newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot gasoline tumbles, Gulf diffs collapse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot gasoline tumbles, Gulf diffs collapse.

text.p: Spot prices for U.S. Gulf Coast conventional unleaded gasoline tumbled five cents a gallon by late Friday as December futures shrank two cents and differentials collapsed amid refiner selling, traders said.
Prompt Gulf "M4" grade was offered by late afternoon at even with the December screen, versus differentials of about 3.50 cents over late Thursday.

"There was plenty of gasoline on offer. Today was scheduling deadline for the front 33rd cycle, so people having barrels for that cycle had to sell it," one trader said. "They came in and sold the market piece by piece."
"It's refiner selling. I knew it was coming. Refineries are back from turnarounds," one Gulf player said.
Among the units back to service is Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Amuay catalytic cracker, which is back to partial production and gearing for full return.
Falling Gulf prices, in turn, helped push New York conventional unleaded one cent lower, with parcels sold for 4.0 cents over December futures, players said.
Heating oil diffs were stable to slightly weaker, traders said, amid a moderate fall in December futures.
